title: The oxytocin/vasopressin receptor antagonist atosiban delays the gastric emptying of a semisolid meal compared to saline in human

what_it_measured.text: The effect of oxytocin and vasopressin on GI motility has to be further evaluated.
The aim of this study was therefore to examine whether oxytocin, or the receptor antagonist atosiban, influence the gastric emptying.

dose.text: It was given as an intravenous bolus dose of 6.75 mg atosiban in a concentration of 7.5 mg/ml,

One ml of Syntocinon® (Novartis, Täby, Sweden), a synthetic analogue to oxytocin, with a concentration of 5 U/ml was dissolved in 250 ml NaCl and given as an intravenous infusion at a rate of 2 ml/min, i.e. a dose of 40 mU/min.

route.text: immediately followed by a continuous intravenous infusion of 5 ml atosiban in a concentration of 7.5 mg/ml dissolved in 250 ml NaCl and given at a rate of 2 ml/min.

endpoint.text: The effect of oxytocin and vasopressin on GI motility has to be further evaluated.
Gastric emptying rate (GER) was assessed and expressed as the percentage reduction in antral cross-sectional area from 15 to 90 min after ingestion of rice pudding.
Ultrasonography Ultrasonographic measurements of gastric emptying were assessed by a standardised method previously described [9].

reported_results.text: Results: Inhibition of the binding of endogenous oxytocin by the receptor antagonist delayed the GER by 37 % compared to saline (p = 0.037).
During infusion of the oxytocin receptor antagonist atosiban, the GER was significantly reduced by 37 % to 36 (22–48) % (Fig 1).

numbers.text: It was given as an intravenous bolus dose of 6.75 mg atosiban in a concentration of 7.5 mg/ml,

One ml of Syntocinon® (Novartis, Täby, Sweden), a synthetic analogue to oxytocin, with a concentration of 5 U/ml was dissolved in 250 ml NaCl and given as an intravenous infusion at a rate of 2 ml/min, i.e. a dose of 40 mU/min.
immediately followed by a continuous intravenous infusion of 5 ml atosiban in a concentration of 7.5 mg/ml dissolved in 250 ml NaCl and given at a rate of 2 ml/min.
Gastric emptying rate (GER) was assessed and expressed as the percentage reduction in antral cross-sectional area from 15 to 90 min after ingestion of rice pudding.
Ultrasonography Ultrasonographic measurements of gastric emptying were assessed by a standardised method previously described [9].
Results: Inhibition of the binding of endogenous oxytocin by the receptor antagonist delayed the GER by 37 % compared to saline (p = 0.037).
During infusion of the oxytocin receptor antagonist atosiban, the GER was significantly reduced by 37 % to 36 (22–48) % (Fig 1).
